prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, your insurance situation, the scope of damage, and which manufacturer warranties you want. I can help you find a great one. Meanwhile, here are practical steps, vetting criteria, and red flags so you can choose confidently.

What to look for
- Insurance/registration: contractor carries general liability and workers’ comp and is registered to do business in Colorado / Denver. Ask for certificates.  
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, etc. These let you get extended manufacturer warranties.  
- Experience with storm claims: a roofer who routinely works with insurance adjusters will speed claims and avoid mistakes.  
- Local reputation: high-rated Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB reviews and local references from Denver homeowners.  
- Written estimates and contracts: itemized scope, materials (brand, color, product line), permit responsibility, start/finish dates, cleanup and disposal, payment schedule, and warranty details (material and workmanship).  
- Permits and inspection: roofer pulls required Denver permits and arranges inspections. (In Denver reroofs typically require permits.)  
- Warranties: verify both manufacturer shingle warranty and a workmanship/installation warranty from the contractor (length and what it covers).  
- Payment terms: reasonable deposit (commonly 10–30%), final payment after job completion and lien waiver. Avoid large up-front cash demands.

Questions to ask a roofer
1. Are you licensed/registered to work in Denver and do you have proof of insurance?  
2. What manufacturer certifications do you have? (Ask for proof.)  
3. How many years doing hail-damage repairs in Denver? Examples of recent jobs nearby?  
4. Will you handle the permit and inspections?  
5. Do you work directly with my insurance company? Can you give an example of an adjuster you worked with?  
6. What brand/model of shingles and underlayment do you recommend and why?  
7. What are your material and workmanship warranties? Are they transferable?  
8. What is the estimated start and completion date? Who will be on site?  
9. Can I see written references or online reviews?  
10. What’s your cleanup plan and will you provide a full lien waiver at final payment?

Red flags (avoid these)
- Door-to-door storm chasers pressuring you to sign immediately.  
- Requests for large cash payments up front (>50%).  
- No local address or no verifiable references.  
- Refusal to pull permits or provide written contract.  
- Very low bid that’s far below others (likely cutting corners or using inferior materials).  
- Asking you to sign over an insurance check.

Where to check reviews and credentials
- Google Maps/Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, BBB.  
- Manufacturer websites for certified contractors lists (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning).  
- Denver Building Department for permit history and local contractor registration.

If you want, I can:
- Help draft a short message/email you can send to multiple roofers to get comparable bids.  
- Help evaluate 2–3 estimates—if you paste the estimates here, I’ll point out differences and which is better value.  
- Narrow a short list if you give your zip code (I can tell you how to find current top-rated local roofers and which search filters to use).

Would you like me to draft an email to send to contractors or help evaluate a couple of quotes? If so, tell me your Denver zip code and whether you’ve already filed an insurance claim.
